Granny Shu looks at your hands rather than your face. ‘You sort faster than the last one. Come in the mornings.’ A cracked jade slip turns over in her fingers. ‘Nobody will have this. Six coin, if you are foolish.’
Cracked jade slip is now known.
Straw pallet is now known.
Straw pallet is now part of your life.
Wen stops counting your sacks aloud. ‘You're on the books now. A small wage comes to you whether you're on my floor or not, and the sacks still pay by the sack. Nobody watches.’

Something that is not air moves under the breath, and it pulls two ways: toward the broken channel beyond the barns, and upstream to a hollow of ferns.

Shu watches you sit through a whole morning's sorting without once fidgeting. ‘So it took,’ she says, and leaves a cup of something bitter by your bundles.

The faint pull from upstream has a shape now. Fernhollow can be sat in.

A flow pattern outlives the broken channel. The water took another course years ago; the qi still turns where it used to bend.

Reset, the stones hum where the flow bends around them. Their spacing supplies exactly the turn the chipped leaf leaves blank.

You take the turn up and it stays, low in the body, like a breath you no longer have to hold. Anything you set out to do next feels shorter already.

Lean-to is now part of your life.
A proper cot is now known.
You shut the lean-to's door behind you for the first time and stand there a while. In Lowbridge, a door you can shut counts as independence.

The carried current spent itself on Settle the foundation.
Settle the foundation: objective complete.

Haul freight to the ferry is now known.

The pooled breath turns, and returns, and turns again without being asked. Foundation. The method has room to grow in it now, and so does the road: the ferry crossing, and the outskirts of Old Ridge beyond it.
A traveller at the ferry asks after whoever cleared the fall. Headman Lu points at you without looking up.
Walk the ridge outskirts is now known.
